lessons.title: L'hiver arrive!
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand that 'hiver' means winter and can identify winter weather signs

opening.activity: Circle time: Students feel ice cubes and fake snow while teacher introduces 'hiver' with shivering gestures. Sing 'Bonjour l'hiver!' greeting song with actions.
materials: Ice cubes in containers (2-3 per pair)
opening.visualSupports: Large winter scene poster, weather gesture cards, 'hiver' word card with picture
decisionPoints: If students hesitate to touch ice: demonstrate with enthusiasm and offer gloves
If energy is low: add more movement with snow falling gestures
If some students are absent: have helpers share materials with newcomers later

main.activity: Winter weather exploration stations: 1) Sensory table with winter textures (10 min), 2) Winter weather sorting with real photos (8 min), 3) 'Je vois l'hiver!' window observation and drawing (9 min). Students rotate in groups of 8.
materials: Sensory bins with ice, fake snow, winter gloves (25 sets)
Laminated weather photo cards (40 cards - winter/not winter)
main.visualSupports: Station instruction picture cards, winter vocabulary poster, temperature gesture reference chart, real winter clothing display
decisionPoints: If sensory station gets crowded: use turn-taking cards with pictures
If sorting is too easy: add 'maybe winter' category for challenge
If drawing time runs short: focus on one winter element per student
movementBreaks: Station transition with 'winter walk' movements (1 min between rotations)

closing.activity: Gallery walk to see all winter drawings. Each student points to their drawing and says 'C'est l'hiver!' with shivering gesture. End with group chant: 'Hiver, hiver, il fait froid!' while doing coordinated movements.
closing.visualSupports: Phrase strip 'C'est l'hiver!', movement demonstration cards, completed winter vocabulary poster
decisionPoints: If students are shy about sharing: start with volunteers and use partner system
If time runs over: have 3-4 students share with promise others share tomorrow
movementBreaks: Group winter movement chant with actions

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding 'hiver' concept or afraid of cold sensory materials
troubleshooting.then: Use warm/cold comparison with safe items (warm mittens vs cold metal spoon), show summer vs winter photos, allow observation without touching, pair with confident peers

lessons.realWorldConnection: Winter brings changes in weather, clothing, and activities that affect daily life

pourDifficultés: Provide hand-over-hand support for materials
Use simpler winter/not winter sorting with obvious pictures
Allow verbal responses in English if needed
Give extra time at each station
pourAvancés: Challenge to find winter details in photos
Encourage complete French sentences
Ask to help classmates with vocabulary
Add descriptive words to drawings
pourLangue: Pair with French-speaking buddy
Use home language to confirm understanding
Provide extra visual supports
Focus on gesture communication
pourPEI: Adapt materials for fine motor needs
Provide sensory alternatives if needed
Use individualized communication supports
Allow movement breaks as needed

observable: Student shows recognition when hearing 'hiver'
Student participates in sensory exploration
Student attempts winter gesture or word
Student shows understanding through sorting or drawing
checkpoints: Can student identify winter weather in photos?
Does student attempt French vocabulary?
Is student engaged with winter sensory materials?
Can student connect 'hiver' to cold/winter concept?

lessons.title: Que porte-t-on en hiver?
lessons.oneGoal: Students can name 3 winter clothing items in French

opening.activity: Mystery box activity: Students reach into winter clothing mystery box, feel items, and guess what they are. Teacher models putting on each item saying 'Je mets mon manteau', etc.
materials: Sample winter clothes: manteau, mitaines, tuque (child sizes)
opening.visualSupports: 'Mystery Box' sign with pictures, winter clothing vocabulary cards with gestures
decisionPoints: If students are hesitant to feel in box: demonstrate first and use transparent box
If items are too difficult to identify: give clues with gestures and pictures
If excitement level too high: use turn-taking cards and quiet voices signal

main.activity: Winter clothing dress-up dramatic play centers: 1) Clothing sort and match game (8 min), 2) Dress-up station with mirrors and role-play (10 min), 3) 'Before/After Winter' drawing comparison (9 min). Groups of 8 students rotate.
materials: Real winter clothing collection (25 pieces total)
Drama props: sunglasses, beach ball, snow shovel
main.visualSupports: Clothing gesture cards, seasonal clothing picture chart, station instruction cards with visuals, vocabulary word strips with actions
decisionPoints: If dress-up station gets chaotic: add 'clothing helper' roles and turn-taking system
If sorting is too easy: add 'sometimes' category for spring/fall clothes
If students finish drawing early: encourage adding details and French labels
movementBreaks: Fashion show walk between stations (1 min)

closing.activity: Winter fashion show: Each student wears one winter item and walks the 'runway' saying 'Je porte mon/ma...' Class responds with applause and 'Très bien!' End with group chant about staying warm.
materials: Upbeat French music for fashion show
Winter clothing items for each student
closing.visualSupports: Sentence strip 'Je porte mon/ma...', applause gesture cards, fashion show photo examples
decisionPoints: If students are shy about modeling: start with confident volunteers and use buddy system
If pronunciation is difficult: accept close attempts and model correct pronunciation
movementBreaks: Fashion show runway walk with music

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty with clothing vocabulary or distinguishing winter vs summer items
troubleshooting.then: Use real demonstration (teacher putting on actual coat), focus on obvious contrasts (shorts vs snow pants), use temperature gestures (shivering vs fanning), provide picture cues

lessons.realWorldConnection: People wear special clothes to stay warm during winter

pourDifficultés: Focus on just one clothing item (manteau)
Use real items with obvious differences
Provide hand-over-hand support for dress-up
Accept pointing instead of verbal responses
pourAvancés: Learn additional clothing items (bottes, foulard)
Create complete French sentences
Help others with clothing vocabulary
Add descriptive words (warm, soft, red)
pourLangue: Connect to home language clothing words
Use visual clothing charts
Pair with bilingual buddy
Focus on gesture and demonstration
pourPEI: Adapt clothing for easy manipulation
Use larger clothing items if fine motor challenging
Provide extra time for dress-up activities
Use preferred communication method

observable: Student attempts to name winter clothing in French
Student can distinguish winter from summer clothes
Student participates in dress-up activities
Student uses gestures to show understanding
checkpoints: Can student identify manteau, mitaines, tuque?
Does student understand when to wear winter clothes?
Can student demonstrate putting on winter items?
Is student engaged in clothing vocabulary activities?

lessons.title: Activités d'hiver amusantes
lessons.oneGoal: Students can identify winter activities they can do outside

opening.activity: Action guessing game: Teacher demonstrates winter activities through exaggerated movements (skating, sledding, building snowman). Students guess and join in the movements, learning vocabulary through action.
opening.visualSupports: Large winter activity picture cards, movement demonstration poster, vocabulary action cards
decisionPoints: If students are confused by movements: use more obvious actions and add verbal clues
If energy gets too high: use 'freeze dance' signals and calming gestures
If some students don't participate: invite them to be 'activity judges' and point to correct pictures
movementBreaks: All opening is movement-based with winter activity actions

main.activity: Winter activity simulation stations: 1) 'Patiner' - sliding with socks on smooth surface (9 min), 2) 'Glisser' - cardboard sled pretend sledding course (9 min), 3) 'Jouer dans la neige' - cotton ball snowball safe play (9 min). Groups of 8 rotate.
materials: Smooth floor area marked for 'skating rink'
Large cardboard pieces for pretend sleds (8)
Cotton balls (200) in bins for snowballs
3 station setup areas with clear boundaries
main.visualSupports: Station picture instruction cards, safety reminder posters, winter activity vocabulary chart, real winter activity photos for inspiration
decisionPoints: If skating station becomes unsafe: switch to seated 'skating' or reduce number of participants
If snowball station gets chaotic: add 'gentle throws only' rule and practice targets first
If students don't understand activity: demonstrate each station before rotation
movementBreaks: Built into activity - constant movement at each station
Station transition with activity-themed movements (1 min walks)

closing.activity: Winter activity choice circle: Each student picks their favorite activity card and demonstrates the action saying 'J'aime...' Group responds 'C'est amusant!' End with group 'Activités d'hiver' chant with all movements combined.
closing.visualSupports: 'J'aime...' sentence starter poster, activity choice cards with pictures, group chant visual with movements
decisionPoints: If students repeat same activity: encourage trying different ones but allow personal preference
If demonstrations become too long: use timer and encourage quick actions
movementBreaks: Group movement chant combining all activities

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding winter activity concepts or having difficulty with movement activities
troubleshooting.then: Use video examples of real children doing activities, provide seated alternatives for movement challenges, focus on one activity at a time, use peer demonstrations

lessons.realWorldConnection: Winter offers unique outdoor activities and fun experiences

pourDifficultés: Focus on one activity (glisser)
Provide seated alternatives for movement
Use hand-over-hand guidance for actions
Accept pointing to pictures instead of demonstrations
pourAvancés: Learn additional activities (skier, faire du hockey)
Create activity sequences or combinations
Teach classmates activity vocabulary
Add safety rules discussion
pourLangue: Connect to activities done in home country
Use universal movement language
Provide home language activity names for comparison
Focus on action rather than verbal expression
pourPEI: Adapt movements for physical abilities
Provide alternative participation methods
Use preferred sensory activities
Allow observation participation if needed

observable: Student recognizes winter activity vocabulary
Student participates in movement activities
Student can demonstrate understanding through actions
Student shows enthusiasm for winter activities
checkpoints: Can student identify glisser, patiner, jouer actions?
Does student participate in station activities safely?
Can student express preference for winter activity?
Is student engaged with movement-based learning?

lessons.title: Animaux en hiver
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand how animals prepare for and survive winter

opening.activity: Animal sound and movement warm-up: Teacher plays animal sounds (bear growl, bird chirping) and students guess the animal, then move like that animal. Introduce concept: 'What do animals do in winter?'
materials: Animal sound audio clips or app
opening.visualSupports: Large animal picture cards (bear, birds, deer), winter scene backdrop poster, 'Animaux en hiver' title card
decisionPoints: If students have trouble identifying animals: show picture with sound simultaneously
If movement gets too energetic: use 'quiet animal movements' and smaller gestures
If some animals are unfamiliar: stick to common local animals students know
movementBreaks: Animal movement imitations (bears walking, birds flying, deer jumping)

main.activity: Animal winter survival discovery centers: 1) 'Hibernation Station' - bears sleeping/denning with cozy materials (9 min), 2) 'Migration Station' - birds flying south with maps and movement (9 min), 3) 'Winter Animal Dress-up' - how animals stay warm (9 min).
materials: Soft blankets and pillows for bear den (hibernation station)
World map showing bird migration routes
Animal winter coats: fake fur pieces, feathers
Before/after animal photos (summer vs winter coats)
3 station setup tables with clear labels
Magnifying glasses for examining fur/feather textures
main.visualSupports: Station instruction cards with pictures, animal winter behavior poster, vocabulary cards with actions, real animal photos showing winter adaptations
decisionPoints: If hibernation station becomes too comfortable (students want to nap): use timer and 'wake up bear' game
If migration concept is confusing: use simple 'birds go where it's warm' and point to warmer places
If dress-up station gets chaotic: implement turn-taking cards and 'animal helper' roles

closing.activity: Animal winter theater: Students choose favorite animal adaptation and demonstrate with simple French phrase: 'L'ours dort en hiver' or 'Les oiseaux volent au sud.' Class responds with animal appreciation sounds.
closing.visualSupports: French animal phrases poster with pictures, performance cue cards, animal adaptation summary chart
decisionPoints: If students are shy about performing: offer partner performances or group demonstrations
If French phrases are too difficult: accept gestures with single words (ours, dormir)

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding animal winter survival concepts or confusing different animal behaviors
troubleshooting.then: Use simple contrasts (animals that sleep vs animals that go away), focus on one animal behavior per lesson, use real photos and videos, connect to pets or familiar animals

lessons.realWorldConnection: Animals have special ways to survive cold winter weather

pourDifficultés: Focus on one animal (ours/bear) and one behavior (dormir/sleep)
Use lots of gestures and movements
Provide simple picture choices
Allow English explanations with French vocabulary
pourAvancés: Learn additional animals (renard, lapin, écureuil)
Discuss multiple survival strategies
Compare different animal adaptations
Help explain concepts to classmates
pourLangue: Connect to animals from students' home countries
Use universal animal sounds and movements
Provide visual animal behavior cards
Encourage home language discussion with French vocabulary
pourPEI: Adapt activities for sensory needs
Provide alternative ways to show understanding
Use preferred animals or focus areas
Allow quiet participation in group activities

observable: Student shows understanding of animal winter behaviors
Student participates in animal movement activities
Student attempts animal vocabulary in French
Student demonstrates care and interest in animals
checkpoints: Can student explain what bears do in winter (dormir)?
Does student understand that birds go somewhere warm?
Can student identify animals by winter behaviors?
Is student engaged with animal survival concepts?

lessons.title: Célébrations autour du monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students discover that many cultures celebrate during winter season

opening.activity: Celebration show-and-tell: Display photos of diverse winter celebrations. Ask 'How does your famille célébrer in winter?' Students share using pictures, gestures, or simple words. Introduce concept of winter célébrations worldwide.
materials: Diverse cultural celebration photo collection (15-20 photos)
opening.visualSupports: World celebration photo display, 'célébration' word card with pictures, family activity picture prompts
decisionPoints: If students don't understand 'célébration': use birthday party as familiar example, add party hats and cake pictures
If students are hesitant to share: provide choice cards with different celebration activities
If discussion goes too long: use timer and promise to continue later

main.activity: Cultural celebration discovery centers: 1) 'Lumières' station - safe exploration of lights in celebrations (9 min), 2) 'Famille Together' - family celebration photo matching and discussion (9 min), 3) 'Celebration Sounds' - music and sounds from winter festivals (9 min).
materials: Battery-operated string lights, LED candles, paper lanterns
Light-up toys and safe illuminated objects
Family celebration photos from diverse cultures (30 photos)
Matching activity boards with celebration scenes
Audio player with cultural celebration music
Headphones or speakers for music station
main.visualSupports: Station instruction cards with cultural respect guidelines, vocabulary posters with celebration images, world map showing celebration locations, appreciation phrases poster
decisionPoints: If lights station becomes overstimulating: dim room lights and provide calming alternatives
If family photos are too personal/sensitive: focus on public celebration images
If music is too loud/unfamiliar: provide volume control and familiar pieces mixed in

closing.activity: Celebration appreciation circle: Each student chooses one celebration photo and shares 'C'est une belle célébration!' Group responds 'Très belle!' End with simple gratitude circle acknowledging all cultures celebrate.
materials: Individual celebration photo cards (25 different ones)
closing.visualSupports: 'C'est une belle célébration!' phrase poster, appreciation gesture cards, cultural respect reminder chart
decisionPoints: If students choose same celebrations: encourage exploring different ones but allow preferences
If French phrase is difficult: accept 'Belle!' or gestures with enthusiasm

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding cultural celebration concept or showing bias toward unfamiliar celebrations
troubleshooting.then: Connect to familiar celebrations first (birthdays, holidays they know), emphasize 'all celebrations are special', use positive language about differences, focus on universal elements (families, food, happiness)

lessons.realWorldConnection: Many cultures have special celebrations during winter months

pourDifficultés: Focus on familiar celebration elements (food, family, lights)
Use simple comparison to known celebrations
Provide picture choices for responses
Allow pointing and gestures for participation
pourAvancés: Learn celebration names from different cultures
Compare celebration similarities and differences
Ask deeper questions about celebration meaning
Help explain celebration concepts to classmates
pourLangue: Connect to home country celebration traditions
Use celebration photos from students' cultures when possible
Allow home language sharing about celebrations
Focus on universal celebration elements
pourPEI: Adapt for sensory sensitivities (especially lights and sounds)
Provide alternative participation methods
Use celebration elements that match student interests
Allow quiet observation participation

observable: Student shows appreciation for different cultural celebrations
Student attempts celebration vocabulary in French
Student participates respectfully in cultural exploration
Student makes connections between celebrations and families
checkpoints: Can student identify elements of celebrations (famille, lumières)?
Does student show respect and curiosity about different cultures?
Can student understand that all cultures have special times?
Is student engaged with multicultural learning?

lessons.title: Noël autour du monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore how Christmas is celebrated in different French-speaking countries

opening.activity: Christmas mystery box: Students reach into box to feel Christmas items (pinecone, small wrapped box, tinsel) while hearing 'Petit Papa Noël' playing softly. Guess items and learn 'Noël' through familiar Christmas elements.
materials: Christmas items: pinecones, small wrapped boxes, safe tinsel, artificial tree branch
opening.visualSupports: Christmas vocabulary picture cards, 'Noël' word card with festive images, mystery box instruction pictures
decisionPoints: If students are hesitant about mystery box: show items first, then put back for feeling
If Christmas music is unfamiliar: pause to explain it's French Christmas music

main.activity: French Christmas exploration stations: 1) 'Sapin de Noël' decorating with French ornament styles (10 min), 2) 'Cadeaux' wrapping practice with French gift customs (8 min), 3) 'Noël en France' photo exploration and simple crafts (9 min). Groups of 8 rotate.
materials: Small artificial Christmas trees (3) for decorating
Small boxes and wrapping materials (25 sets)
Photos of Christmas in France, Quebec, Belgium
Simple Christmas craft supplies: paper, colors, stickers
main.visualSupports: Station instruction cards in French and pictures, Christmas vocabulary posters, French Christmas tradition photos, cultural Christmas comparison charts
decisionPoints: If tree decorating becomes unbalanced: assign 'decoration director' role to students
If wrapping is too difficult: pre-made practice boxes and simpler materials
If cultural photos are confusing: compare to familiar Christmas elements first
movementBreaks: Christmas tree decorating reaching and stretching

closing.activity: Christmas sharing circle: Students hold their wrapped gifts or ornaments and say 'Joyeux Noël!' to the group. Practice French Christmas greeting exchange. End with quiet group singing of 'Petit Papa Noël' chorus.
closing.visualSupports: 'Joyeux Noël!' greeting poster, Christmas sharing picture examples, song lyrics with visual supports
decisionPoints: If students are shy about greeting: model with enthusiastic examples and use buddy pairs
If singing is too difficult: focus on 'Joyeux Noël' phrase repetition

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students from non-Christmas celebrating families feeling excluded or confused about Christmas vocabulary
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize learning about how others celebrate, compare to any family celebrations they have, focus on universal elements (giving, family time, special foods), allow observation participation

lessons.realWorldConnection: Christmas is celebrated differently around the world, including in French-speaking countries

pourDifficultés: Focus on one Christmas element (sapin)
Use familiar Christmas concepts first
Provide hand-over-hand support for crafts
Accept pointing to Christmas items
pourAvancés: Learn additional Christmas vocabulary (étoile, couronne)
Compare French vs local Christmas traditions
Help explain Christmas customs to classmates
Create more complex Christmas crafts
pourLangue: Connect to Christmas celebrations in home countries
Use Christmas images as universal language
Compare Christmas words in different languages
Focus on visual Christmas elements
pourPEI: Adapt Christmas activities for sensory needs
Provide alternative participation in Christmas exploration
Use preferred Christmas elements or focus areas
Allow quiet observation of Christmas activities

observable: Student recognizes Christmas vocabulary (Noël, sapin, cadeaux)
Student participates respectfully in Christmas cultural exploration
Student attempts French Christmas greetings
Student shows understanding of Christmas as cultural celebration
checkpoints: Can student identify basic Christmas elements?
Does student attempt 'Joyeux Noël' greeting?
Can student participate in Christmas-themed activities?
Is student respectful of Christmas cultural learning?

lessons.title: Hanoukka - Festival des lumières
lessons.oneGoal: Students learn about Hanukkah as a winter celebration of lights

opening.activity: Light counting game: Show pictures of menorahs and count candles together 'un, deux, trois...huit!' Use finger counting and demonstrate adding one candle each day. Introduce 'Hanoukka' as festival of lights.
materials: Battery-operated menorah or LED demonstration model
opening.visualSupports: Number chart with French words, menorah picture sequence, 'Hanoukka' vocabulary card with lights
decisionPoints: If counting in French is too difficult: accept counting in any language with French number support
If students are unfamiliar with menorahs: explain as 'special candleholder for celebration'

main.activity: Hanukkah learning centers: 1) 'Menorah Making' - paper menorah craft with 8 candles (12 min), 2) 'Hanukkah Story' - simple picture book exploration (8 min), 3) 'Light Festival' - safe light play and appreciation (7 min). Groups of 8-9 students.
materials: Yellow and orange paper for candle flames
Glue sticks and safety scissors (25 sets)
Battery-operated candles and safe LED lights
Light table or bright lamp for light exploration
main.visualSupports: Menorah craft instruction cards with pictures, Hanukkah story visual supports, light safety reminder posters, respectful learning guidelines
decisionPoints: If craft is too complex: pre-cut pieces and focus on assembly and decoration
If students have questions about Hanukkah: keep explanations simple and age-appropriate about family celebrations

closing.activity: Menorah sharing circle: Students hold their paper menorahs and count 'huit' candles together. Practice saying 'Happy Hanoukka!' in French and appreciate the beautiful lights everyone made.
closing.visualSupports: 'Happy Hanoukka' greeting poster, counting support chart, light appreciation vocabulary
decisionPoints: If French Hanukkah greeting is too difficult: focus on 'huit' counting and light appreciation

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not familiar with Hanukkah or having difficulty with religious/cultural concept
troubleshooting.then: Focus on universal elements (families celebrating, lights being beautiful, special times together), compare to any light celebrations they know, emphasize learning about how others celebrate

lessons.realWorldConnection: Hanukkah is an important winter festival celebrating religious freedom and miracles

pourDifficultés: Focus on light and counting concepts
Simplify menorah craft with pre-made pieces
Use concrete counting with real objects
Accept gesture responses for participation
pourAvancés: Learn about Hanukkah traditions beyond lights
Help classmates with menorah crafts
Practice French numbers beyond huit
Ask thoughtful questions about celebrations
pourLangue: Compare light festivals from different cultures
Use home language to discuss celebrations
Focus on visual and hands-on activities
Connect to light celebrations they may know
pourPEI: Adapt craft activities for fine motor needs
Provide sensory alternatives if needed
Use preferred learning methods
Allow flexible participation in group activities

observable: Student shows respect for Hanukkah as cultural celebration
Student attempts to count to huit in French
Student participates in menorah craft activity
Student demonstrates understanding of lights as celebration element
checkpoints: Can student identify menorah as special light holder?
Does student show curiosity and respect about Hanukkah?
Can student count candles or participate in number activities?
Is student engaged with multicultural learning about light festivals?

lessons.title: Kwanzaa - Célébration africaine-américaine
lessons.oneGoal: Students discover Kwanzaa as a cultural winter celebration

opening.activity: Color exploration activity: Display red, black, and green objects. Students sort classroom items by these trois couleurs while teacher introduces 'Kwanzaa uses these special colors.' Count 'sept' days with finger counting.
materials: Red, black, and green objects from classroom (blocks, crayons, toys)
opening.visualSupports: Kwanzaa color chart with meanings (simple), 'sept' number card with French, Kwanzaa family celebration photos
decisionPoints: If students have difficulty with color sorting: provide obvious color choices and model first
If sept counting is challenging: use familiar objects to count to seven
movementBreaks: Counting to sept with finger exercises

main.activity: Kwanzaa learning stations: 1) 'Kinara Candles' - seven candle arrangement with colors (10 min), 2) 'Community Helpers' - matching people helping in community (8 min), 3) 'Kwanzaa Crafts' - simple red, black, green art project (9 min). Groups rotate.
materials: Red, black, green construction paper strips for candles
Community helper photo cards (police, teachers, doctors, etc.)
Glue sticks and safety scissors (25 sets)
main.visualSupports: Kinara instruction cards with pictures, community helper vocabulary posters, Kwanzaa color meaning chart (simplified), station instruction cards
decisionPoints: If kinara concept is confusing: compare to other celebration candle holders (menorah, birthday candles)
movementBreaks: Kinara candle arrangement reaching and placing

closing.activity: Community appreciation circle: Students hold their Kwanzaa crafts and share one way people help in community. Count 'sept' candles together and appreciate community helpers with applause.
closing.visualSupports: Community helper visual prompts, 'sept' counting poster, appreciation gesture cards
decisionPoints: If students struggle with community helper concept: provide specific picture choices (teacher, parent, friend helping)

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding Kwanzaa cultural significance or community values concept
troubleshooting.then: Focus on helping others and being kind (universal values), use familiar community helpers, emphasize that all cultures have special celebrations, connect to family helping and caring

lessons.realWorldConnection: Kwanzaa celebrates African-American culture and community values

pourDifficultés: Focus on color recognition and counting sept
Use concrete community helper examples
Simplify craft to color sorting activity
Accept gesture or pointing responses
pourAvancés: Learn more about community values and helping
Help explain Kwanzaa elements to classmates
Create more detailed kinara crafts
Discuss additional ways to help community
pourLangue: Connect to community helpers in home countries
Use universal helping gestures and actions
Focus on visual community helper cards
Allow home language discussion of helping others
pourPEI: Adapt activities for individual needs
Use preferred community helper examples
Modify crafts for fine motor abilities
Provide alternative ways to show understanding of helping others

Student can identify red, black, green Kwanzaa colors

checkpoints: Can student recognize Kwanzaa colors and count to sept?
Does student show understanding of people helping each other?

lessons.title: Diwali d'hiver et autres fêtes
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore other cultural celebrations that can happen in winter

opening.activity: Light exploration game: Show different types of lights (flashlight, LED candle, lantern photos). Students identify which gives light and learn 'lanternes' as special light holders. Introduce concept of light celebrations in dark winter.
materials: Various safe light sources (flashlight, LED candles, lamp)
opening.visualSupports: Light source picture cards, 'lanternes' vocabulary card with images, cultural light celebration photos
decisionPoints: If students are overstimulated by lights: use gentler lighting and provide warning
If lantern concept is unfamiliar: compare to familiar light sources like lamps or candles
movementBreaks: Light holding and gentle waving movements

main.activity: Cultural light celebration stations: 1) 'Beautiful Lanternes' - simple paper lantern craft (12 min), 2) 'Light Traditions' - photos and stories of different light festivals (8 min), 3) 'Winter Light Play' - safe light exploration and shadows (7 min).
materials: Colored tissue paper and construction paper
Battery-operated tea lights for completed lanterns
Glue sticks and safety scissors (25 sets)
Simple picture books about light celebrations
White wall or sheet for shadow projections
main.visualSupports: Lantern craft instruction cards, cultural light tradition pictures, shadow play safety posters, celebration appreciation vocabulary
decisionPoints: If lantern craft is too complex: pre-cut pieces and focus on decorating and assembly

closing.activity: Lantern celebration circle: Students hold their completed lanterns (with LED lights) and share in darkened room. Each says one thing they learned about light celebrations. End with appreciation of all beautiful 'traditions'.
materials: Completed student lanterns with LED lights
closing.visualSupports: 'Traditions' vocabulary poster, celebration appreciation phrases, lantern sharing example pictures
decisionPoints: If darkened room is uncomfortable for some students: keep some ambient lighting and allow students to stay in brighter areas
movementBreaks: Gentle lantern holding and showing movements

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by multiple cultural celebrations or not understanding light celebration concepts
troubleshooting.then: Focus on lights being beautiful and special, compare to birthday candles or holiday lights they know, emphasize that people like to celebrate with pretty lights, keep explanations simple and visual

lessons.realWorldConnection: Many cultures have light-based celebrations during dark winter months

Accept pointing and gesture responses

Compare different types of lanternes and lights
Help classmates with lantern crafts
Ask thoughtful questions about light traditions
pourLangue: Connect to light celebrations from home cultures
Use light as universal celebration element
Allow sharing in home language about light traditions
Focus on hands-on light exploration

Provide sensory alternatives if light sensitivity
Use preferred participation methods
Allow flexible engagement with light activities

lessons.title: Nouvel An autour du monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students discover different New Year celebrations and traditions

opening.activity: Calendar exploration: Show current calendar and point to 'nouvelle année' dates. Students practice saying 'nouveau' with new vs old object comparisons (new crayon vs used crayon). Make wishes with 'souhaits' gestures.
opening.visualSupports: 'Nouvelle année' calendar visual, 'nouveau/vieux' comparison poster, 'souhaits' gesture cards with pictures
decisionPoints: If calendar concept is confusing: focus on 'new day' vs 'old day' and birthdays as familiar 'new year' concept
If 'souhaits' is too abstract: use 'happy thoughts' and wishing on stars examples

main.activity: New Year celebration stations: 1) 'Noise Maker Crafts' - creating celebration shakers and horns (12 min), 2) 'New Year Around World' - photos and cultural exploration (8 min), 3) 'Wishes and Hopes' - drawing and sharing positive thoughts (7 min).
materials: Paper plates, dried beans, rice for shakers
Global New Year celebration photo collection
Simple New Year traditions picture books
main.visualSupports: Noise maker craft instruction cards, world New Year celebration map, wish-making picture prompts, cultural celebration photos with simple explanations
decisionPoints: If noise makers become too loud: establish 'quiet celebration' and 'loud celebration' times
movementBreaks: Noise maker testing and gentle celebration dancing

closing.activity: New Year celebration finale: Students use their noise makers for gentle 'Bonne année!' celebration. Share one wish or happy thought. End with group countdown 'trois, deux, un... Bonne année!' with cheering.
closing.visualSupports: 'Bonne année!' greeting poster, countdown visual support, celebration gesture cards
decisionPoints: If celebration becomes too energetic: use calming countdown and quiet celebration voices

lessons.title: Cuisine d'hiver réconfortante
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore comfort foods and special dishes from winter celebrations

opening.activity: Warm and cold food sorting: Present pictures of foods and drinks. Students sort into 'chaud' (warm/hot) and 'froid' (cold) categories. Introduce winter comfort foods that warm us up, focusing on 'soupe' as warm food.
materials: Food picture cards (mix of hot and cold foods)
Real examples: warm soup picture, ice cream picture
opening.visualSupports: Hot/cold food sorting chart, 'soupe' vocabulary card with steaming bowl, temperature gesture reference poster
decisionPoints: If students struggle with hot/cold concept: use real warm and cold objects to demonstrate temperature first
If food sorting is too easy: add 'sometimes hot, sometimes cold' category for foods like milk

main.activity: Winter comfort food stations: 1) 'Soupe Kitchen' - pretend soup making with safe materials (10 min), 2) 'Chocolat Chaud' - hot chocolate sensory exploration (8 min), 3) 'Biscuits and Treats' - winter treat sorting and pretend baking (9 min).
materials: Play kitchen setup with pots, spoons, ladles
Soup ingredient pictures and play vegetables
Hot chocolate powder for safe smelling
3 station setup areas with clear boundaries
main.visualSupports: Soup making instruction picture cards, hot chocolate vocabulary poster, biscuit types chart, cultural comfort food photos
decisionPoints: If soup station gets messy: provide more structured containers and limit water amount

closing.activity: Comfort food sharing circle: Students choose favorite winter comfort food picture and share 'J'aime la soupe' or 'J'aime le chocolat.' Group responds 'Mmm, c'est bon!' End with gratitude for warm, delicious food.
closing.visualSupports: 'J'aime...' sentence starter poster, comfort food appreciation cards, gratitude and thankfulness visual supports
decisionPoints: If students choose same foods repeatedly: encourage trying different ones but respect preferences

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students with food allergies or restrictions feeling excluded from food activities
troubleshooting.then: Focus on looking and smelling rather than tasting, use play food and pictures prominently, emphasize that all families have different special foods, include diverse cultural comfort foods

lessons.realWorldConnection: Special foods and warm drinks are important parts of winter celebrations

pourDifficultés: Focus on familiar comfort foods (soup, hot chocolate)
Use real food examples and pictures
Simplify to hot/cold sorting activity
Accept pointing to preferred foods
pourAvancés: Learn additional winter food vocabulary (pain, fromage)
Discuss cooking processes and ingredients
Help classmates with food vocabulary
Compare comfort foods from different cultures
pourLangue: Connect to comfort foods from home cultures
Use food pictures as universal language
Allow sharing food names in home language
Focus on sensory food experiences
pourPEI: Adapt for food allergies and sensitivities
Provide alternative sensory experiences if needed
Use preferred food examples
Allow observational participation in food activities

lessons.title: Musique et chansons d'hiver
lessons.oneGoal: Students learn songs and music from different winter celebrations

opening.activity: Musical instrument exploration: Present various instruments (bells, shakers, drums). Students identify which make 'musique' and practice gentle playing. Introduce 'chanson' by humming familiar tune and having students guess.
materials: Simple musical instruments: bells, shakers, small drums
Audio clips of familiar tunes for guessing
opening.visualSupports: Musical instrument identification poster, 'musique' and 'chanson' vocabulary cards, instrument playing demonstration pictures
decisionPoints: If instruments are too loud: establish 'gentle music' rule and model soft playing
If song guessing is too difficult: use very familiar songs like 'Happy Birthday' or 'Twinkle Twinkle'

main.activity: Winter music exploration stations: 1) 'Chanson Learning' - simple French winter songs with actions (10 min), 2) 'Cultural Music' - listening and moving to winter celebration music (8 min), 3) 'Dance and Movement' - winter celebration dancing (9 min).
materials: French winter song sheets with pictures
Audio recordings of simple French winter songs
Cultural winter music collection (Christmas, Hanukkah, etc.)
Simple rhythm instruments for each student
Cultural dance photos and video examples
main.visualSupports: Song lyrics with picture supports, cultural music identification cards, dance movement instruction pictures, respectful listening poster
decisionPoints: If French songs are too complex: focus on simple repeated phrases and lots of actions
movementBreaks: All activities are movement-based: singing with actions, cultural dancing, rhythmic movements

closing.activity: Winter music concert: Students choose their favorite song or music from the lesson and perform for the group (humming, dancing, or playing instruments). Audience responds with gentle applause and appreciation.
materials: Student choice of instruments or scarves
Music from lesson for background support
closing.visualSupports: Performance choice cards, audience appreciation gesture cards, concert etiquette poster
decisionPoints: If students are shy about performing: offer group performances and encourage simple movements or humming
movementBreaks: Individual or small group performances with movement

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by musical activities or reluctant to participate in singing/dancing
troubleshooting.then: Offer alternative participation (listening, gentle swaying, instrument holding), respect cultural or personal comfort levels with music/dance, provide quieter musical activities, focus on enjoyment over performance

lessons.realWorldConnection: Music and songs are essential parts of cultural celebrations

pourDifficultés: Focus on listening and simple movements
Use familiar tune patterns with French words
Provide visual song supports with lots of pictures
Accept any form of musical participation
pourAvancés: Learn complete verses of French winter songs
Help teach songs to classmates
Create original winter song verses
Lead group musical activities
pourLangue: Connect to musical traditions from home cultures
Use music as universal language
Allow singing in home language mixed with French
Focus on rhythm and movement over lyrics
pourPEI: Adapt for sensory sensitivities to music volume/types
Provide alternative ways to participate in musical activities
Use preferred musical elements or instruments
Allow quiet participation or observation

Student shows appreciation for different cultural music
Student demonstrates understanding that music is part of celebrations
checkpoints: Can student identify chanson, musique, danser concepts?

lessons.title: Créons nos décorations
lessons.oneGoal: Students create winter celebration decorations from different cultures

opening.activity: Decoration discovery box: Students explore box filled with colorful decoration materials (ribbons, shiny paper, beads). Practice 'couleurs' vocabulary by sorting materials and learn 'décorer' by adding items to plain classroom objects.
materials: Ribbons, shiny paper, safe beads, stickers
opening.visualSupports: Color vocabulary poster, 'décorer' action demonstration cards, before/after decoration examples
decisionPoints: If materials are overwhelming: present smaller amounts and add more gradually
If color sorting is too easy: add patterns and texture sorting
movementBreaks: Decoration material exploration and sorting movements

main.activity: Cultural decoration creation stations: 1) 'Christmas Decorations' - stars and snowflakes (9 min), 2) 'Hanukkah Decorations' - blue and white crafts (9 min), 3) 'Multicultural Celebration' - diverse cultural decoration making (9 min).
materials: White, silver, gold paper and materials
Red, black, green materials for Kwanzaa-style crafts
Glue sticks, safety scissors, markers (25 sets)
main.visualSupports: Cultural decoration photo examples, step-by-step craft instruction cards, respectful cultural representation guidelines, color-meaning reference charts
decisionPoints: If crafts are too complex: provide pre-cut pieces and focus on decorating and assembly
movementBreaks: Station transition with decoration appreciation walks

closing.activity: Decoration celebration gallery: Students display their decorations around room and take appreciation walk, saying 'C'est beau!' to classmates' work. End with group appreciation of all cultural decorations created.
closing.visualSupports: 'C'est beau!' appreciation poster, cultural decoration appreciation guidelines, respectful viewing behavior cards
decisionPoints: If gallery walk becomes chaotic: use structured pairs and designated viewing order

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students making cultural decorations they don't celebrate or feeling excluded from certain cultural crafts
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize learning about and appreciating different cultures, focus on universal decoration elements (beauty, colors, creativity), allow students to make decorations from their own traditions, celebrate all cultural contributions equally

lessons.realWorldConnection: People decorate their homes and communities for winter celebrations

Use decoration as universal creative language

lessons.title: Notre festival d'hiver multiculturel
lessons.oneGoal: Students participate in a classroom winter celebration festival

opening.activity: Festival preparation circle: Students gather to see all their winter celebration work displayed around room. Practice 'partager' by sharing one favorite memory from winter celebration learning. Introduce 'festival' as special celebration time 'ensemble'.
materials: All student work from previous lessons displayed
opening.visualSupports: Winter celebration learning journey photo display, 'festival' vocabulary card with celebration images, 'partager' and 'ensemble' action cards
decisionPoints: If students have trouble remembering activities: use photo prompts and specific lesson artifacts

main.activity: Multicultural winter festival celebration: Students rotate through celebration stations featuring all cultures studied - Christmas corner, Hanukkah area, Kwanzaa station, New Year celebration, winter foods, music, and decorations. Each station has activities from previous lessons.
materials: All decorations created in previous lessons
Musical instruments and songs from lesson 12
Food pictures and pretend food from lesson 11
main.visualSupports: Station identification signs with pictures, cultural celebration summary posters, respectful celebration participation guidelines, multicultural appreciation displays
decisionPoints: If festival becomes overwhelming: provide quiet celebration spaces and reduce stimulation levels

closing.activity: Unity celebration circle: All students gather with one item from festival (decoration, instrument, picture). Each says 'Toutes les célébrations sont belles!' Group responds 'Oui, c'est beau ensemble!' End with group appreciation of winter celebration learning journey.
materials: Student choice of festival items to hold
closing.visualSupports: Unity celebration phrase poster, multicultural appreciation chart, celebration gratitude cards
decisionPoints: If French phrases are too complex: accept enthusiastic 'C'est beau!' and focus on appreciation gestures

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling overwhelmed by multiple cultural elements or preferring one culture over others
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize that all celebrations are special and different families celebrate differently, provide breaks from stimulation, focus on common elements (family, joy, gratitude), allow students to participate at comfort level

lessons.realWorldConnection: Communities often hold winter festivals celebrating cultural diversity

pourDifficultés: Focus on familiar festival elements
Provide structured station participation with support
Use simple celebration vocabulary
Allow observation participation when needed
pourAvancés: Help facilitate festival stations
Explain cultural celebrations to younger students if available
Lead group in multicultural appreciation activities
Create connections between different celebrations
pourLangue: Highlight celebrations from students' home cultures when possible
Use festival as celebration of cultural diversity including their backgrounds
Allow sharing in home languages during festival
Focus on universal celebration joy
pourPEI: Adapt festival participation to sensory and social needs
Provide quiet celebration alternatives
Use preferred celebration elements
Allow flexible participation in group festival activities

lessons.title: Histoires d'hiver magiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore winter stories and legends from different cultures

opening.activity: Story circle magic: Students sit in cozy circle with dim lighting and winter scene backdrop. Teacher introduces story time with 'Il était une fois...' (Once upon a time) and shows beautiful winter story illustrations. Students practice story listening position.
materials: Dim lighting setup (lamps instead of overhead)
opening.visualSupports: 'Il était une fois' story starter card, story listening behavior poster, winter story covers display
decisionPoints: If students are too excited for calm story time: use calming music and breathing exercises first

main.activity: Winter story exploration: Teacher reads 2-3 short winter stories from different cultures, pausing for student predictions and connections. Students use story props to act out favorite parts and create story illustrations.
materials: Story prop basket: artificial snowflakes, stars, winter animals, lights
Drawing paper and crayons for story illustrations
Cultural winter storybooks from different countries
main.visualSupports: Story prediction picture cards, cultural story comparison chart, story element identification posters, winter story vocabulary with pictures
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne connaît pas d'histoires d'hiver → encourager à parler de sa propre famille ou inventer une histoire simple
Si les livres sont trop difficiles → utiliser les images pour raconter l'histoire en français simple
Si l'attention diminue → ajouter des gestes et des voix de personnages

closing.activity: Story sharing circle: Students show their story illustrations and share one word or phrase from their favorite winter story. Group appreciates each story with gentle 'applause rain' (finger tapping).
closing.visualSupports: Story sharing sentence starters, appreciation gesture cards, favorite story vocabulary support
decisionPoints: Si un élève est timide pour partager → commencer par pointer une image et dire 'J'aime ça!'
Si le temps manque → choisir 3-4 histoires préférées pour partager demain
Si les élèves parlent tous en même temps → utiliser le bâton de parole avec rappel 'Chacun son tour'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty sitting for stories or understanding story concepts in French
troubleshooting.then: Use more visual stories with pictures, allow movement during stories, provide story props for hands-on engagement, accept English responses with French vocabulary support

lessons.realWorldConnection: Cultures share winter stories that teach values and traditions

Focus on story enjoyment over comprehension

Ask to help retell stories to classmates
Create original story endings
Learn additional story vocabulary
pourLangue: Use universal story elements and visual supports
Connect to similar stories from home cultures
Allow story discussion in home language
Focus on story emotions and actions
pourPEI: Provide comfortable seating and positioning
Use preferred story themes or characters
Allow movement during story time if needed
Adapt story activities to individual communication needs

lessons.title: Jeux d'hiver intérieurs
lessons.oneGoal: Students play traditional winter games from different cultures

opening.activity: Game discovery time: Show pictures of children playing different winter games around the world. Students guess how each game is played through gestures and movements. Introduce concept of 'jeux' (games) that keep people happy during winter.
opening.visualSupports: 'Jeux d'hiver' vocabulary poster, game identification pictures, movement gesture cards
decisionPoints: Si les élèves devinent trop rapidement → ajouter des indices plus subtils avec des gestes
Si un jeu n'est pas familier → demander si quelqu'un connaît ce jeu ou un jeu similaire
Si l'énergie est très haute → utiliser des signaux calmes et la voix chuchotée
movementBreaks: Game guessing movements and gestures throughout opening

main.activity: Cultural winter game stations: Students rotate through 3 adapted traditional games - simple board game from one culture, movement game from another, and cooperative game from third culture. Each game adapted for indoor classroom play.
materials: Game pieces and boards for 8 students
Cooperative game materials (rope, parachute, or large cloth)
main.visualSupports: Game instruction cards with pictures and simple words, cultural game origin posters, cooperation and fair play reminder cards
decisionPoints: If games become too competitive or chaotic: emphasize fun and cooperation over winning, modify rules for gentler play

closing.activity: Game appreciation circle: Each student demonstrates one movement or action from their favorite game played today. Group tries to guess which game and culture it represents. End with appreciation for all games and cultures.
materials: Cultural game reference cards for guessing
closing.visualSupports: Game demonstration cards, cultural appreciation posters, 'favorite game' sharing prompts
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne veut pas démontrer → offrir de faire équipe ou juste observer cette fois
Si les démonstrations prennent trop de temps → limiter à 2 minutes par jeu avec minuterie visuelle
Si les élèves se disputent les jeux → utiliser un système de rotation avec numéros

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students becoming too competitive or frustrated with unfamiliar games
troubleshooting.then: Focus on fun and trying new things rather than winning, simplify game rules, emphasize cooperation and learning about different cultures, provide alternative participation methods

lessons.realWorldConnection: Winter games help people stay active and connected during cold months

Provide partner support during games
Focus on participation rather than game mastery
Use familiar game elements when possible
pourAvancés: Learn more complex game rules and strategies
Help explain games to classmates
Create variations or combinations of games
Research origins and cultural significance of games
pourLangue: Use games as universal play language
Connect to similar games from home cultures
Focus on movement and action rather than verbal instructions
Allow game discussion in home language
pourPEI: Adapt game rules and materials for individual abilities
Provide alternative participation methods

lessons.title: Cartes de vœux multiculturelles
lessons.oneGoal: Students create greeting cards for different winter celebrations

opening.activity: Greeting card exploration: Show beautiful example cards from different cultures and celebrations. Students practice different cultural greetings with gestures. Introduce card-making as way to share celebration wishes with others.
opening.visualSupports: Multicultural greeting card display, greeting gesture reference chart, card-giving etiquette pictures
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne célèbre pas ces fêtes → inclure des cartes de gentillesse générale comme 'Bonne journée!'
Si les salutations sont difficiles à prononcer → accepter les tentatives et modeler doucement
Si un élève est timide avec les gestes → commencer par un simple sourire et 'Bonjour!'

main.activity: Multicultural card creation workshop: Students choose which cultural celebration card to make, then create personalized greeting cards using appropriate cultural symbols, colors, and greetings. Focus on respectful representation and personal creativity.
materials: Card-making station with folded card blanks (25)
Cultural color collections (red/green, blue/white, red/black/green, etc.)
Greeting phrase strips in French and other languages
main.visualSupports: Cultural symbol and color meaning charts, greeting phrase pronunciation guides, respectful cultural representation guidelines, card-making instruction steps
decisionPoints: Si un élève trouve la création difficile → offrir des pochoirs ou des autocollants simples
Si les matériaux se mélangent → utiliser des plateaux individuels avec noms
Si un élève termine rapidement → encourager à faire une carte bonus pour la famille

closing.activity: Card sharing and gifting circle: Students present their cards and practice giving them with appropriate cultural greetings. Exchange cards with classmates or prepare to take home to families. Appreciate diversity of celebrations represented.
closing.visualSupports: Card presentation and gifting etiquette poster, cultural greeting reference, appreciation and gratitude visual supports
decisionPoints: Si un élève oublie les mots → chuchoter doucement ou utiliser des gestes d'aide
Si l'échange devient chaotique → utiliser un système de partenaires organisé
Si un élève reçoit beaucoup de cartes → s'assurer que tout le monde en reçoit au moins une

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students unsure about representing cultures they don't celebrate or making cards for unfamiliar celebrations
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize making cards to learn about and honor different cultures, focus on showing respect and appreciation, allow students to make cards for celebrations they're curious about, connect to universal themes of kindness and celebration

lessons.realWorldConnection: People send cards and greetings to share celebration wishes

Use preferred cultural themes or celebrations

lessons.title: Spectacle de talents d'hiver
lessons.oneGoal: Students perform songs, dances, or stories from winter celebrations

opening.activity: Talent show warm-up: Students practice being good audience members with gentle applause, appreciation gestures, and encouraging faces. Review performance options from winter celebration unit and let students choose their talent to share.
opening.visualSupports: Good audience behavior poster, performance option visual menu, encouragement gesture cards
decisionPoints: Si un élève n'a pas d'idée de talent → suggérer des options simples comme montrer un jouet ou faire un sourire spécial
Si quelqu'un a le trac → offrir de présenter avec un ami ou juste montrer aux enseignants
Si le temps de pratique est court → encourager des talents de 30 secondes maximum

main.activity: Winter celebration talent show: Students take turns performing their chosen talents - songs, dances, stories, or demonstrations from different winter celebrations. Each performance celebrated with audience appreciation and cultural context sharing.
materials: Performance area with simple stage setup
Props from previous lessons (instruments, scarves, etc.)
Cultural context cards for each celebration
main.visualSupports: Performance stage area, cultural celebration context posters, audience appreciation reminders, performance encouragement displays
decisionPoints: If students are nervous about performing: offer partner performances, group participation, or alternative ways to share (showing, explaining, helping others)
movementBreaks: All performances involve movement, singing, dancing, or demonstration

closing.activity: Talent show celebration finale: Group appreciation circle where each performer receives specific positive feedback. End with group celebration of all talents shared and cultures represented. Document special moments.
closing.visualSupports: Appreciation feedback prompts, group celebration posters, performance celebration visual supports
decisionPoints: Si un élève ne veut pas performer → encourager à être un super public avec applaudissements spéciaux
Si les performances dépassent le temps → garder les extras pour un spectacle bonus demain
Si un élève fait des commentaires négatifs → rappeler 'Nous encourageons nos amis' avec geste positif

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students too nervous to perform or audience becoming restless or critical
troubleshooting.then: Offer alternative participation methods (helping, explaining, partnering), reinforce positive audience behaviors, keep performances short and varied, celebrate effort and participation over skill level

lessons.realWorldConnection: Performance and entertainment are important parts of cultural celebrations

pourDifficultés: Offer simple performance options (showing an item, humming a tune)
Allow partner or group performances
Focus on participation and effort over performance quality
Provide alternative ways to contribute (helping others, being excellent audience)
pourAvancés: Encourage more complex performances combining multiple elements
Ask to help less confident performers
Add cultural explanation to their performances
Take leadership roles in talent show organization
pourLangue: Allow performances in home language with cultural sharing
Use performance as universal expression beyond language
Encourage sharing cultural performances from home traditions
Focus on non-verbal performance options
pourPEI: Adapt performance expectations to individual abilities and interests
Provide alternative participation methods
Use preferred performance styles or comfort levels

lessons.title: Interview avec les familles
lessons.oneGoal: Students interview family members about their winter celebration traditions

opening.activity: Family connection introduction: Students share photos or drawings of their families celebrating. Practice interview skills with simple questions like 'What do you like?' and good listening. Introduce concept of learning from family knowledge.
materials: Family photos or drawings from students
opening.visualSupports: Family celebration photo examples, interview question picture cards, good listening behavior poster
decisionPoints: Si un élève n'a pas de photos de famille → utiliser des dessins ou parler de personnes spéciales
Si les célébrations sont très différentes → célébrer cette diversité avec 'Que c'est intéressant!'
Si un élève ne veut pas partager → respecter ce choix et offrir d'écouter les autres

main.activity: Family interview preparation and practice: Students prepare interview questions, practice with partners, and create documentation materials to take home. Role-play respectful family interviews and prepare to share findings with class.
materials: Family interview question templates with pictures
Documentation sheets for recording family traditions
main.visualSupports: Family interview question cards with pictures, respectful questioning guidelines, family tradition documentation templates, cultural appreciation posters
decisionPoints: Si les questions d'entrevue sont trop difficiles → simplifier à 'Qu'est-ce que tu aimes?' ou utiliser images
Si un partenaire est absent → faire l'entrevue en trio ou avec l'enseignant
Si la pratique devient bruyante → utiliser des voix de souris et des signaux visuels

closing.activity: Interview commitment and sharing preview: Students commit to interviewing one family member about winter traditions. Share excitement about learning family stories. Plan for sharing findings in future lessons.
closing.visualSupports: Family interview commitment poster, sharing preview visual supports, family appreciation and gratitude cards
decisionPoints: Si les familles ne peuvent pas participer → offrir d'interviewer un membre du personnel ou utiliser photos
Si un élève oublie l'entrevue à la maison → lui donner une autre chance ou faire une entrevue en classe
Si l'excitation est très haute → canaliser avec des gestes de calme et respiration profonde

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students from families who don't celebrate winter holidays or students uncomfortable with family interview concept
troubleshooting.then: Expand to include any family traditions, seasonal activities, or special memories, allow students to interview community members or friends, focus on family storytelling and connection rather than specific celebrations

lessons.realWorldConnection: Families are the primary source of cultural celebration knowledge

lessons.title: Calendrier de célébrations d'hiver
lessons.oneGoal: Students create a winter celebration calendar showing diverse cultural celebrations

opening.activity: Learning journey reflection: Display all student work from winter celebration unit around the room. Students take appreciation walk to remember all celebrations learned. Introduce calendar as way to organize and remember celebration learning.
materials: All student work from previous 19 lessons displayed
opening.visualSupports: Winter celebration learning journey display, calendar concept introduction poster, celebration memory prompts
decisionPoints: Si les élèves sont excités par tous les souvenirs → utiliser 'J'observe' silencieux d'abord puis partager
Si quelqu'un ne trouve pas ses œuvres → aider à chercher ensemble ou célébrer le travail d'un ami
Si le temps d'appréciation est long → limiter à 2 commentaires positifs par élève

main.activity: Collaborative winter celebration calendar creation: Students work together to create large class calendar marking all celebrations studied. Add decorations, pictures, and cultural elements for each celebration. Include family traditions shared from interviews.
materials: Decoration materials from all celebrations studied
Student artwork and crafts from previous lessons
main.visualSupports: Cultural celebration date reference charts, calendar creation instruction cards, celebration timeline visual supports, multicultural calendar examples
decisionPoints: Si la création du calendrier devient chaotique → assigner des sections spécifiques à chaque groupe
Si les matériaux se mélangent → utiliser des bacs étiquetés par mois avec photos
Si certains élèves dominent → utiliser un système de rotation 'Chacun ajoute une chose'

closing.activity: Calendar celebration and unit reflection: Present completed class winter celebration calendar. Students share favorite memory from winter celebration learning. Celebrate accomplishment of learning about many cultures and traditions.
closing.visualSupports: Unit accomplishment poster, reflection sharing prompts, celebration and gratitude visual supports
decisionPoints: Si les élèves sont tristes que l'unité se termine → planifier comment continuer les célébrations tout l'hiver
Si la présentation du calendrier prend trop de temps → chaque élève dit une chose qu'il a apprise
Si quelqu'un n'a pas participé beaucoup → trouver quelque chose de positif qu'il a fait pour le célébrer

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by amount of celebration information or difficulty remembering all celebrations learned
troubleshooting.then: Focus on favorite celebrations or most memorable activities, use photo prompts and artifacts to support memory, emphasize that learning about different cultures is ongoing journey, celebrate effort and curiosity

lessons.realWorldConnection: Calendars help communities plan and remember important cultural celebrations

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: "Célébrations d'hiver"

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en français
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
L'hiver arrive!, Que porte-t-on en hiver?, Activités d'hiver amusantes, Animaux en hiver, Célébrations autour du monde

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Il est normal et bénéfique que votre enfant mélange les langues à la maison.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

Merci pour votre soutien continu dans l'apprentissage du français!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
